title: U.S. House · Georgia's 11th District
area: Northwest Atlanta suburbs and exurbs, including Cartersville, Woodstock, and parts of Cherokee and Bartow counties.

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Barry Loudermilk (R) is not running for re-election. John Cowan won the Republican primary runoff over Rob Adkerson on June 16, 2026. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball rate the general election Solid/Safe Republican.

candidates.name: John Cowan
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 16 Republican primary runoff over Rob Adkerson, 65.0%

summary.text: John Cowan is the Republican nominee in Georgia's 11th Congressional District. A Cartersville native, he is a neurosurgeon who describes himself as a small-business owner and a "conservative outsider." He ran unsuccessfully for Georgia's 14th District in 2020 and won the June 16, 2026 Republican runoff for the open 11th District seat.

background.text: According to his campaign website, his family has been part of the Bartow County community since the 1930s; his father was a physician and his mother a schoolteacher, and he grew up on the family farm and graduated from Cartersville High School.

Graduated from Davidson College with a B.S. in physics, received an M.D. from the Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, and completed a neurosurgery residency at the University of Michigan Medical School.
Works as a neurosurgeon and says he has cared for patients for over 20 years; he also describes himself as a small-business owner who has built businesses creating jobs in the district.
As of his 2020 campaign, Ballotpedia listed him as founder of Cortex Toys and Cortex Holdings.
Ran in the 2020 Republican primary for Georgia's 14th District and lost the August 11, 2020 runoff to Marjorie Taylor Greene.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary and won the June 16, 2026 runoff over Rob Adkerson, 65.0% to 35.0%.
According to his campaign website, he and his wife, Dr. Anne Cowan, are raising four children and are active in their church, where he serves as an elder.

priorities.text: Supports term limits for members of Congress and a total ban on congressional stock trading.

Says he will work to "rein in reckless federal spending, lower the cost of living for American families... secure our border and elections, and put patients — not politicians — back in charge of their own medical care."

positions.summary: His campaign site says he would require proof of citizenship to vote.
positions.quote: Require proof of citizenship to vote

statements.quote: Preserve and protect our constitutional rights to free speech, freedom of worship, and the right to bear arms.
Fix the problems created by Obamacare — lower premiums, expand choices, and put patients back in charge of their own care.
President Trump is securing the border. Congress needs to back him up.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: We have to cut federal spending, slash taxes, unleash American energy, and end burdensome regulations.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

summary.text: Chris Harden is the Democratic nominee in Georgia's 11th Congressional District. A Rossville native, he is an attorney who co-owns an estate-planning and probate firm in Woodstock and has spent about 13 years as a contract attorney handling juvenile-court dependency cases for Georgia counties. He is running on lowering costs, healthcare, and government accountability.

background.text: Born in Rossville, Georgia, and graduated from Ridgeland High School; says he grew up in a working-class family and is the oldest of three siblings.

Earned an associate degree from Chattanooga State Technical Community College (2005), a bachelor's degree from Georgia State University (2009; political science/pre-law), and a law degree from Atlanta's John Marshall Law School (2012).
According to his campaign website, he worked full time, including driving a forklift and loading trucks, while attending school at night.
Passed the bar and was sworn in to practice law in 2012.

Has worked about 13 years as a contract attorney taking appointed juvenile-court dependency cases, representing parents or children, for Walker, Catoosa, Dade, Chattooga, DeKalb, Gordon, Bartow and now Cherokee counties.
Co-owns the Harden Law Firm, LLC, an estate-planning and probate practice in Woodstock, with his wife, Amber.
Lives in Cherokee County with his wife and their five-year-old triplets, according to his survey responses.
Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary for the open seat.

priorities.text: Says government should pursue "practical, balanced solutions — not partisan fights."
Supports strengthening public education, including retaining teachers and ensuring students have needed resources.
Wants to lower healthcare and prescription drug costs and expand coverage access, especially in rural and underserved communities.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will fight to restore and expand the enhanced ACA premium tax credits and protect and strengthen Medicare and Medicaid.
positions.quote: Chris will fight to restore and expand those credits so families are not hit with higher premiums because Congress fails to act.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he believes reproductive freedom is a fundamental right and that women should have access to abortion care.
positions.quote: Chris believes reproductive freedom is a fundamental right.

positions.summary: His campaign site says he will fight for middle-class tax relief while ensuring large corporations and the wealthiest Americans contribute their fair share.
positions.quote: ensuring that large corporations and the wealthiest Americans contribute their fair share

positions.summary: His campaign site says he supports raising the minimum wage.
positions.quote: he supports raising the minimum wage so that a full day’s work can support a stable life

positions.summary: His campaign site says he supports modernizing the electric grid and expanding clean-energy development.
positions.quote: expanding clean-energy development that can lower long-term energy costs, create good jobs, and strengthen American competitiveness

summary.text: Natalie Richoz is a registered nurse running as a write-in independent for Georgia's 11th Congressional District. Born in Marietta, she says she has lived in the district for more than 50 years and is a brain-tumor survivor. She campaigns on healthcare reform and on protecting Social Security, veterans' benefits, and Medicare and Medicaid.

background.text: Born in Marietta, Georgia; Ballotpedia lists a diploma from Cass High School, a degree from Chattahoochee Technical College (2006), and an associate degree from Georgia Highlands College (2010).
Career experience listed on Ballotpedia includes work as a registered nurse, construction assistant, food service assistant and retail employee.
Describes herself as a wife, mother and grandmother who completed nursing school to earn an RN, and says she has lived in north Georgia's District 11 for more than 50 years.
Is now disabled after surviving a brain tumor, requiring surgery and radiation treatment; says the experience gave her a first-hand view of healthcare from both the provider and patient perspectives.
Is a write-in independent candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Says Social Security, veterans' benefits, and Medicare/Medicaid should not be placed "onto the chopping block of Congress," and that the district's lower-income households face increasing difficulty finding affordable housing.
priorities.quote: We the People of District 11 deserve to be placed above special interest groups, business tax exemptions and billionaire bailouts. It is our civic duty as representatives of the people to ensure that what CITIZENS invest in for their futures is never placed onto the chopping block of Congress again. These include but are not limited to Social Security, Veteran Benefits and Medicare/Medicaid.

priorities.text: Says healthcare is her "driving force" and that patients, not Big Pharma or insurers, should be the highest priority.
priorities.quote: Patients, American citizens, should be our highest priority... not Big Pharma, Medical or exorbitant insurance premiums.

priorities.text: Supports term limits, saying there should be no "life appointments" in Congress.

positions.summary: Proposes a single-payer national health insurance program that expands Medicare to cover every U.S. resident.
positions.quote: This is our collective American proposal for our single-payer national health insurance program that would expand and retool traditional Medicare to cover every U.S. resident automatically from cradle to grave.

positions.summary: Says Congress should consider wealth taxes, taxes on unrealized gains and closing loopholes to reduce the national debt.
positions.quote: We are wise to integrate solutions that include wealth taxes (levy on all assets)

positions.summary: Says raising the minimum wage would be a first step.
positions.quote: raising the minimum wage will be the first step

statements.quote: This cannot happen very easily with our government starting global conflicts and Congress remaining inactive in their Constitutional check of those powers.
Together, we will work to heal our community’s shortage of affordable housing and encourage economic growth that benefits us all.
Immigration reform to boost a Constitutionally secure labor supply and entrepreneurship is crucial.

summary.text: Amanda Carter James is a Cartersville native running as a write-in independent for Georgia's 11th Congressional District. She has worked 35 years for Shaw Industries, currently as a Senior Fabrication Manager in product development, and has been a registered mediator for 12 years.

background.text: Describes herself as a lifelong Georgian and Cartersville native, a mother of three and a grandmother of one.

Graduated from Cartersville High School (1985); attended Florida A&M University and earned a B.S. in Political Science with a concentration in Public Service and Policy from Kennesaw State University (2015, per Ballotpedia).
Has worked 35 years for Shaw Industries, currently as a Senior Fabrication Manager for Hard Surface in Product Development, and has been a registered mediator for 12 years.
Is a write-in independent candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election.

priorities.text: Says rising food and housing costs are "causing financial strain on families in District 11" and pledges to work to lower those costs.
Says healthcare and prescription drug costs are "bankrupting American families."
Says she wants to focus on mental health, calling for increased insurance coverage of mental health care and more school counselors and resources.

positions.summary: Says she would introduce legislation to expand healthcare marketplace tax credits and increase competition to lower prescription drug and insurance costs.
positions.quote: I aim to rectify these issues by introducing legislation to expand healthcare marketplace tax credits, increase out of state competition, and initiate policies to diminish the collusion by the pharmaceutical companies and the government.

statements.quote: Population within our communities has increased, exponentially, which impacts the housing shortage; thereby increasing the rental and mortgage rates.
statements.context: In her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey
